scenes.headline: Break-even day. Still lost $1,400.
scenes.say: Break-even day. And you still lost fourteen hundred dollars.

scenes.headline: The limit chases your high.
scenes.say: With an intraday trailing limit, it follows your highest balance, open profit included.

scenes.headline: Then it never comes down.
scenes.say: The trade goes back to zero. The limit doesn't. Two thousand of room is now six hundred.

scenes.title: Want the guide to every limit type?
scenes.sub: Comment it. I'll DM you the free guide.

post.instagram:
On an intraday trailing drawdown the loss limit follows your highest balance, open profit included. A 50K account with a $2,000 limit runs to +$1,400 open: the limit rises to $49,400. The trade comes back to break-even and the limit stays there: $600 of room left instead of $2,000. Some firms trail end-of-day instead, and most limits lock at some point: check your firm's rules. Comment RULES for the free guide.
